title: STRONG AND COURAGEOUS TO THE END

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Lord gave this command to Joshua son of Nun: 'Be strong and courageous, for you will bring the Israelites into the land I promised them on oath, and I myself will be with you.'" — Deut 31:23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now God Himself speaks directly to Joshua the words that have echoed throughout this chapter: "Be strong and courageous... I myself will be with you." First Moses spoke these words to Joshua, and now God confirms them with His own voice. What an encouragement that must have been — to hear the very promise of courage sealed by God personally.

Notice again the foundation of the courage: "I myself will be with you." Joshua's strength was never meant to come from his own abilities, his experience, or his confidence. It came from the promise of God's presence. This is the secret of every faithful servant of God — not self-reliance, but reliance on the God who goes with us.

It is worth pausing on how God gives Joshua a clear task alongside the promise: "you will bring the Israelites into the land." Courage is not vague optimism; it is trusting God as we step forward into the specific work He has given us. God's presence and God's calling go together.

This same promise belongs to all who follow Christ. Before Jesus sent His disciples into the daunting task of reaching the world, He gave them the identical assurance: "I am with you always" (Matt 28:20). Whatever God has called you to do, however daunting it feels, He does not send you alone. Be strong and courageous — not because the task is easy or because you are capable, but because the God who calls you goes with you to the very end.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What task has God given me that requires courage right now?
2. Is my courage resting on my own ability, or on God's presence?
3. How does "I am with you always" strengthen me for what I face?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You call me to courage and then promise Your own presence. Help me not to rely on myself but on You. Be with me in the task before me, and make me strong in You. Amen.
